bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42473836 (capstonenext): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target fuzz_disasmnext [msan].
bug_description.normalized: MCInst_Init does not initialize the x86opsize field of the MCInst structure. When disassembling an X86 BND instruction (e.g., BNDLDX) with a memory operand, printanymem does not set x86opsize for BND opcodes, so the field remains uninitialized. printMemReference reads the uninitialized x86opsize and copies it to op1_size. The tainted op1_size is then read in X86_Intel_printInst, triggering a use-of-uninitialized-value.

source.code: r = handle->disasm(ud, buffer, size, &mci, &insn_size, offset, handle->getinsn_info);
source.description: X86 disassembler decodes attacker-controlled bytes into MCInst mci, producing a BNDLDXrm opcode while x86opsize remains uninitialized.
source.value_from: attacker-controlled PoC bytes passed from LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput via cs_disasm buffer parameter
source.note: The X86 disassembler decodes the PoC bytes (0x0f 0x1a 0x1a = BNDLDX) into the mci MCInst struct; the instruction is decoded successfully (r=true) but mci.x86opsize was never initialized by MCInst_Init and is not set during decoding.

sink.description: Conditional read of MI->op1_size that carries the uninitialized x86opsize value, flagged by MSan as use-of-uninitialized-value.
sink.note: Reads MI->op1_size in a conditional. The value is tainted with the uninitialized x86opsize from printMemReference, causing MSan to flag the use-of-uninitialized-value.

root_cause.description: MCInst_Init omits initialization of x86opsize, leaving the field with indeterminate stack contents that propagate through printMemReference to the sink.
root_cause.note: MCInst_Init initializes op1_size, Opcode, size, has_imm, writeback, ac_idx, popcode_adjust, assembly, and wasm_data, but omits x86opsize. The field remains uninitialized on the stack.

tainted_value_origin.note: Stack allocation of mci. The x86opsize field is not initialized by MCInst_Init and retains indeterminate stack contents.

parser_admitted.code: r = handle->disasm(ud, buffer, size, &mci, &insn_size, offset, handle->getinsn_info);
parser_admitted.note: X86 disassembler successfully decodes PoC bytes as BNDLDX instruction.

coarse_trace.summary: Initializes most MCInst fields but omits x86opsize, leaving it uninitialized.
Disassembles PoC input as BNDLDX instruction; calls the printer function pointer (X86_Intel_printInst) with the mci whose x86opsize is uninitialized.
Dispatches on MI->Opcode to set x86opsize for LEA instructions, but BNDLDXrm has no case, so x86opsize remains uninitialized; calls printMemReference.
Reads MI->x86opsize (uninitialized) into operand size and copies it to MI->op1_size.
Reads the tainted MI->op1_size in a conditional, triggering use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: MCInst_Init sets op1_size=0 but does not initialize x86opsize. The field retains indeterminate stack contents from the mci allocation in cs_disasm.

fine_trace.code: r = handle->disasm(ud, buffer, size, &mci, &insn_size, offset, handle->getinsn_info);
fine_trace.note: Disassembler decodes the PoC bytes 0x0f 0x1a 0x1a as a BNDLDXrm instruction. Decoding succeeds (r=true), populating mci.Opcode but not setting mci.x86opsize.

printanymem dispatches on MI->Opcode. BNDLDXrm matches only the default case (break), so MI->x86opsize is not set. Only LEA opcodes have entries. Falls through to call printMemReference with x86opsize still uninitialized.
Reads uninitialized MI->x86opsize and stores it into the memory operand's size field. This propagates the uninitialized taint to the operand detail structure.

Copies the uninitialized MI->x86opsize into MI->op1_size. The previously-initialized op1_size (set to 0 by MCInst_Init) is overwritten with the tainted value. Guarded by if (MI->op1_size == 0), which is true since op1_size was 0.
Reads MI->op1_size in a comparison. The value is tainted with the uninitialized x86opsize from step 5. MSan detects the use-of-uninitialized-value here.

poc.trigger: The 4-byte PoC (0x00 0x0f 0x1a 0x1a) selects X86 32-bit Intel syntax (byte 0 = 0x00, platform index 0) and encodes a BNDLDX memory instruction (bytes 0x0f 0x1a with ModR/M 0x1a). The fuzzer calls cs_disasm which decodes this as BNDLDXrm, triggering the uninitialized x86opsize read path.

format.name: raw_x86
format.contract: First byte selects architecture/mode (0x00 = X86 32-bit Intel); remaining bytes are raw X86 machine code containing a BNDLDX instruction (opcode 0x0f 0x1a) with a memory operand.
